model: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route)

inputs.base_revenue_basis: FY2025 rental income (EUR m, FY2025 AR / H1 2026 report outlook table). Rental income is the DRIVER line only -- it is the one top-line Vonovia guides (FY2026: EUR 3.45-3.55bn) and the Rental segment is ~87% of Adjusted EBITDA. The flow that is valued is attributable AFFO (see last_fcf_note), expressed as a margin on rental income. CSV total revenue (FY2025 4,749.3) includes Development and Recurring Sales gross proceeds and is not used as the driver.
inputs.share_count_basis: 848,435,117 registered no-par shares at 30-Jun-2026 (H1 2026 report, Share Information), all carrying dividend rights (EPRA NTA per share 46.22 = 39,212.0 / 848.4). Held FLAT: the FY2025 dividend (EUR 1.25, EUR 1,060.5m) was paid fully in cash in 2026 with no scrip (equity statement), so the 2025 scrip-driven rise from 822.9m to 848.2m is not repeated in the base. Convertible bonds (incl. the EUR 850m 2026 placement) are struck far above the current price and are excluded from the diluted count; conversion would be mildly NTA-accretive, not dilutive, at those strikes. SBC (EUR 11.6m, largely cash-settled LTIP) is expensed inside Adjusted EBT so no further dilution is modelled.
inputs.net_debt_note: Deliberately ZERO in the model. The flow capitalised is attributable AFFO, which is already AFTER the adjusted net financial result (FY2025 EUR -739.9m; LTM Jun-26 EUR -782.9m) and after distributions to non-controlling interests. Deducting the EUR 40,024m balance-sheet net debt on top would charge the debt twice (dcf-methods SKILL.md: never capitalise a post-interest flow and then subtract net debt). total_debt and cash below are recorded for audit only. Leverage context at 30-Jun-2026: non-derivative financial liabilities 42,233.6; cash incl. term deposits 2,172.7; net debt 40,024.0; LTV 46.0% (covenant <60%, company target ~40% by 2028); adjusted net debt / adjusted EBITDA 14.0x; ICR 3.6x; average cost of debt ~2.1% guided to drift up ~20bp/yr as low-coupon debt refinances; ratings BBB+ (S&P, Fitch), Baa1 (Moody's), A- (Scope).
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2025 attributable AFFO (EUR m): Adjusted EBT (continuing operations) 1,904.3 + straight-line depreciation 116.7 - capitalized maintenance 327.1 - income tax payments (w/o taxes on Non Core sales) 229.2 - dividends and payouts to non-controlling shareholders 202.9 = 1,261.8, i.e. EUR 1.49 per share against the EUR 1.25 dividend (84% payout). All five lines are from the Adjusted EBT -> OFCF reconciliation (FY2025 AR, 'Reconciliation of Adjusted EBT (Continuing Operations)/Operating Free Cash-Flow'). The same build on FY2024 gives 1,816.3 + 112.7 - 294.2 - 235.5 - 143.7 = 1,255.6, so attributable AFFO was flat (+0.5%) in 2025. EXCLUDED from the owner flow, although inside Vonovia's own OFCF of 1,778.5: 'Carrying amount of investment properties sold (core business)' 338.5 (return of capital from Recurring Sales -- the asset leaves the rent roll), 'Change in net working capital Development to sell/Manage to Green' 138.3 (timing) and 'Intragroup profit/losses' 39.9 (non-cash cost advantage). Statutory net income (4,185.5 in FY2025, -6,756.2 in FY2023) is dominated by investment-property fair-value movements and is not used anywhere in this valuation.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY2025 Operating Free Cash-Flow (OFCF), Vonovia's own headline cash metric, guided 'at previous year's level' for FY2026 (before changes in net working capital Development to sell/Manage to Green). H1 2026 OFCF was 607.5 vs 1,113.1 in H1 2025, the drop being the working-capital and disposal-timing lines that are excluded from the owner flow above; H1 2026 Adjusted EBT was 962.3 (-2.6% YoY).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 cash-flow statement share-based payment add-back EUR 11.6m (CSV StockBasedComp; FY2024 10.9). It is an expense inside Adjusted EBT and is NOT added back in the AFFO build, so the engine's SBC path is held at 0% to avoid charging it twice; EquityAwardTaxes are 0 in every year. House and street bases therefore coincide (SBC-zero convention) and band_position is null.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2025 interest income EUR 73.3m is left inside the adjusted net financial result (it nets within the -739.9m line) because net debt is not deducted in this model; stripping it would remove income without removing the matching cash.
inputs.wacc_rationale: The 9.0% is a COST OF EQUITY in EUR, not a WACC, because the flow is post-interest. Build: 10-year Bund ~2.8% (late-October 2026 level assumed from the H1 2026 report's rate commentary; refresh when the next filing or a live quote is to hand) + equity risk premium 5.0% x levered beta ~1.2 (46% LTV, 14x adjusted net debt / EBITDA, DAX-40 residential landlord) = 8.8%, rounded to 9.0%. The same rate is used in all three scenarios -- risk is charged once, through the scenario paths and weights, not through per-scenario discount rates. For reference the market price implies roughly 11% on the FY2025 AFFO at 2% growth (1.49 x 1.02 / 16.57 + 2%).
inputs.lease_treatment: Not material: Vonovia is the lessor; right-of-use liabilities (ground leases, offices) are immaterial against EUR 42bn of financial liabilities and their cost is inside Adjusted EBT. No separate lease line.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged ONCE, as a cash outflow: 'Dividends and payouts to non-controlling shareholders' (FY2024 143.7, FY2025 202.9, H1 2026 256.0 vs H1 2025 175.1) is folded into capex_pct_path at 7.0% of rental income in the base (EUR ~245m in FY2026). The NCI are chiefly the 2023 Apollo / CBRE IM minority stakes in the Suedewo, Northern Germany and Baden-Wuerttemberg portfolios (~EUR 3bn of minority capital with preferred-style returns) plus the ~13% Deutsche Wohnen minority (EUR 4,694m NCI equity at 30-Jun-2026). Because the flow is attributable after these payouts, NO NCI deduction is made in the equity bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity, run through the Drivers/engine route (as GPT.AX and GMG.AX). Vonovia is an IAS 40 fair-value residential landlord: net income is revaluation noise, reported FCF/OCF are after modernization and development spend and before disposal proceeds, and 'EBITDA' sits above EUR 0.74-0.78bn of interest on EUR 42bn of debt. The dcf-methods routing table sends IAS 40 property owners to AFFO/distributable-profit capitalisation at the cost of equity with net debt held at zero. ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = rental income; ebitda_margin_path = (Adjusted EBT + straight-line depreciation) / rental income, so that engine EBIT (EBITDA - D&A) equals Adjusted EBT, the pre-tax post-interest earnings Vonovia guides; cash_tax_rate_path = cash income taxes / Adjusted EBT (12.0% FY2025, 13.0% FY2024 -- Vonovia is a normal German corporate taxpayer, not a G-REIT, but tax depreciation, interest deductibility and loss carryforwards keep the cash rate low); da_pct_path = straight-line depreciation / rental income (added back after tax, so it affects only the tax line); capex_pct_path = capitalized maintenance (9.6% FY2025, 8.9% FY2024, H1 2026 +19% YoY) PLUS distributions to NCI (5.9% FY2025) -- both post-tax cash outflows. Modernization (~EUR 1bn+/yr) and new construction are growth capital funded by Recurring Sales, the EUR 2.7bn non-core disposal programme and debt within the LTV target; they are what the organic rent growth path pays for and are not deducted again. FY2025 check: 3,417.2 x 59.15% = 2,021.0 - D&A 116.7 = 1,904.3 Adjusted EBT; -12.0% tax = 1,675.8; +116.7 - 530.0 (327.1 + 202.9) = 1,262.5 = last_fcf (rounding). CROSS-CHECK AGAINST NTA: EPRA NTA per share is EUR 46.22 (30-Jun-2026); the base-case AFFO value sits at roughly half of it, which is the model saying a 9% equity return on a portfolio yielding ~4.0% gross / ~2.85% on Rental EBITDA (2,445 / 85,676) through 46% LTV cannot support the appraised values -- the NTA discount is a finding, not an input. Analysis.json (2026-10-25) was present and read; the price has fallen a further ~23% since the 30-Jun-2026 close of EUR 21.59 with no filing in the folder after the H1 2026 report (29-Jul-2026) to explain it; the Q3 2026 statement (due early November) should be read on the next update.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: rental_income_3yr_cagr (FY2022 3,168.1 -> FY2025 3,417.2), consistent with the FY2026 rental income guidance midpoint (+2.4%) and organic rent growth of ~4% net of a ~1.5%/yr shrinking unit count
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity and NTA per share CAGRs are negative (3yr -4.3% / -7.0%) while rental income and Adjusted EBITDA grew; the gap is the 2022-2024 investment-property fair-value write-downs (EUR -0.6bn, -9.2bn, -0.6bn pre-tax) reversing to +2.5bn in 2025. The 5yr revenue CAGR (9.1%) is the 2021 Deutsche Wohnen acquisition, not organic. EPS is fair-value driven and not a growth series (FY2023 -7.80, FY2025 +4.47); 3yr EPS CAGR is null because the FY2022 base is negative.
historical_growth.notes: fcf_3yr_cagr is the Adjusted EBT CAGR FY2022 1,997.3 -> FY2025 1,904.3 (-1.6%/yr), the longest consistent post-interest series: rising interest costs (adjusted net financial result) absorbed the Adjusted EBITDA growth (2,606.1 -> 2,800.8, +2.4%/yr). Attributable AFFO on the model's definition: FY2024 1,255.6 -> FY2025 1,261.8 (+0.5%); earlier years lack the capitalized-maintenance and NCI-payout lines in the same definition. Discontinued series for context: FFO 1,348.2 (FY2020) -> 1,801.6 (FY2023), 10.1%/yr, inflated by the Deutsche Wohnen consolidation; FFO per share 2.38 -> 2.23 over the same period (-2.1%/yr) is the per-share truth.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 = midpoint of the reaffirmed EUR 3.45-3.55bn rental income guidance (+2.4%; H1 2026 ran at this pace), i.e. ~4% organic rent growth (guidance ~4%) less the rent lost on the ~EUR 2.7bn non-core disposal programme and Recurring Sales. FY2027-2030 at 2.8-3.0% as disposals taper and modernization-linked and indexation increases carry a ~4% organic rate on a flatter unit count, then fading to 2.0% -- German rent regulation (Mietpreisbremse extended to 2029, Kappungsgrenze) keeps like-for-like growth near CPI.
base.margin_rationale: (Adjusted EBT + straight-line depreciation) / rental income. Actuals: FY2022 ~66%, FY2023 ~61%, FY2024 58.0%, FY2025 59.1% -- the fall is the adjusted net financial result rising from ~EUR 0.5bn to 0.74bn. FY2026 58.7% = Adjusted EBT ~EUR 1.93bn (lower half of the EUR 1.9-2.0bn guidance, which management said may be hard to reach at the top after H1's -2.6%) plus ~EUR 125m depreciation on EUR 3.50bn rental income. Thereafter a gentle recovery to 59.5%: Adjusted EBITDA Total growing toward the EUR 3.2-3.5bn 2028 target (value-add to 20-25% of EBITDA) is only partly offset by the ~20bp/yr cost-of-debt drift (~EUR 85m/yr on EUR 42bn) and the interest saved on disposal-funded debt reduction.
base.sbc_note: SBC (EUR 11.6m) is expensed inside Adjusted EBT; see inputs.sbc_source.
base.da_rationale: Straight-line depreciation 116.7 / 3,417.2 = 3.4% in FY2025, 112.7 / 3,323.5 = 3.4% in FY2024; guided 'moderate increase' in FY2026 on photovoltaic and PP&E investment -> 3.6%. D&A is added back after tax, so this line only sets the tax base (EBIT = Adjusted EBT).
base.capex_rationale: Capitalized maintenance 10.0% of rental income (FY2025 9.6%, FY2024 8.9%, H1 2026 141.3 vs 118.8 = +19% YoY) PLUS distributions to non-controlling shareholders 7.0% (FY2025 5.9% = 202.9; H1 2026 256.0 already exceeds the FY2025 run-rate, FY2024 4.3%). Gives FY2026E attributable AFFO ~EUR 1.22bn / EUR 1.44 per share (-3% on FY2025) -- consistent with OFCF guided flat and H1 Adjusted EBT -2.6% -- and 1.15x cover of the EUR 1.25 dividend. Modernization and new construction are growth capital, see inputs.notes.
base.tax_rationale: Income tax payments (w/o taxes on Non Core sales) / Adjusted EBT: 229.2 / 1,904.3 = 12.0% FY2025, 235.5 / 1,816.3 = 13.0% FY2024. 12.5% held flat; the German minimum-tax / RETT share-deal interpretation risk the H1 2026 report raised from <5% to 5-39% probability is carried in the bear path.
base.terminal_note: Gordon at 9.0% / 2.0% = 14.6x terminal AFFO (a 6.9% AFFO yield) binds below the 16x cap. Vonovia trades at ~11x FY2025 attributable AFFO today; listed German residential peers traded at 18-25x FFO in the 2015-2021 low-rate era. 2.0% perpetual growth = CPI-linked indexation under a rent-regulated regime with a slowly shrinking owned portfolio.

bull.growth_rationale: Same FY2026 guidance year; from FY2027 the tenancy-law reform passes without the index-rent cap, organic rent growth holds 4-4.5% (housing shortage, modernization pass-through) and the disposal programme completes early so the unit count stabilises.
bull.margin_rationale: Upper half of the FY2026 Adjusted EBT guidance (EUR ~1.94bn); then Bund yields ease, the EUR 2.7bn+ disposals (including the flagged larger portfolio exit) at close to book take LTV toward the 40% 2028 target and cut the adjusted net financial result, while value-add reaches 20-25% of a EUR 3.4-3.5bn Adjusted EBITDA Total in 2028. Margin recovers toward the FY2023 level (~61%) and beyond, still short of FY2022's ~66%.
bull.capex_rationale: Capitalized maintenance 9.5% + NCI payouts 6.5% (minority structures partly bought out or refinanced as LTV falls).
bull.terminal_note: Gordon at 9.0% / 3.0% = 17.2x binds below the 18x cap; 3.0% is organic rent growth of ~4% less a slowly shrinking stock, the bull's structural case.

bear.growth_rationale: FY2026 at the bottom of the rental income range (EUR 3.45bn, +1.0-2.0%) as disposals accelerate to defend the rating; from FY2027 the cabinet's tenancy-law bill passes WITH the 3% index-rent cap and a tightened Kappungsgrenze, organic rent growth falls to ~2.5-3% and continued forced disposals at a discount to book take 1-1.5%/yr of rent out, leaving net rental growth at 1.5%.
bear.margin_rationale: Adjusted EBT misses the FY2026 range (EUR ~1.89bn, continuing H1's -2.6%); then the ~20bp/yr cost-of-debt drift on EUR 42bn (the H1 2026 report's 'unfavorable interest rate developments' / 'higher refinancing costs' amber risks, EUR 450-900m each) outruns EBITDA growth, Development stays loss-making and disposals shrink the rent base faster than they cut interest. Margin erodes to ~53%, roughly where Adjusted EBT would sit at today's rental income with a EUR 1.0bn financial result.
bear.capex_rationale: Capitalized maintenance 10.5% (GModG / heating-transition and EPBD upgrade costs that cannot be passed through under a tighter modernization levy) + NCI payouts 7.5% (H1 2026 run-rate persists).
bear.tax_rationale: Minimum-tax / RETT share-deal interpretation risk (probability raised to 5-39% in the H1 2026 report) lifts the cash rate to 15%.
bear.terminal_note: Gordon at 9.0% / 1.5% = 13.5x binds below the 14x cap. The bear is a slow grind, not insolvency: ICR stays above the 1.8x covenant and LTV below 60%, so no zero-floor terminal value and no equity raise is modelled -- a dilutive raise to defend BBB+ would be the next leg down and would sit below this case.

scenario_narratives.base: Vonovia stays what it is: a EUR 85bn regulated German residential portfolio earning ~4% organic rent growth on a stock that shrinks ~1-1.5%/yr through Recurring Sales and the EUR 2.7bn non-core programme, so rental income compounds ~2.5-3%. Adjusted EBT tracks the lower half of FY2026 guidance (~EUR 1.93bn) and then grows a little faster than rent as value-add scales toward 20% of EBITDA and disposal proceeds retire debt faster than the ~20bp/yr coupon drift adds interest. Attributable AFFO dips ~3% in FY2026 on higher capitalized maintenance and NCI payouts, then compounds ~3.5%/yr. Capitalised at a 9% EUR cost of equity with 2% perpetual growth the equity is worth roughly half of EPRA NTA -- the market's discount to NTA is partly justified by the leverage-adjusted yield, not entirely a mispricing.
scenario_narratives.bull: Rates ease, the tenancy-law reform passes without the index-rent cap, and the new CEO's two levers both work: the larger portfolio exit and the EUR 2.7bn non-core sales clear near book, taking LTV to the 40% 2028 target and cutting the financial result, while third-party value-add revenue lifts Adjusted EBITDA Total to the EUR 3.4-3.5bn end of the 2028 target. Adjusted EBT per share recovers toward EUR 2.9-3.0 by 2030; the stock re-rates toward the EUR 30.76 average analyst target range. Even here the value stays well below NTA: the model does not pay appraised values for a portfolio yielding 2.85% on Rental EBITDA.
scenario_narratives.bear: The tenancy-law bill passes with the 3% index-rent cap and a tighter Kappungsgrenze, organic rent growth falls toward 2.5-3%, and Vonovia -- unable to delever through rent -- sells faster and at a discount to book to hold the BBB+ rating. Interest costs on EUR 42bn drift up 20bp a year with no offsetting EBITDA growth, Development stays loss-making, the GModG / EPBD retrofit burden lifts capitalized maintenance, and the minimum-tax interpretation raises cash tax. Attributable AFFO settles around EUR 1.1bn (~EUR 1.30/share), the dividend is held or trimmed, and the equity is worth about today's price. A dilutive rights issue to protect the rating is the tail below this case and is not modelled.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 35%: 14.0x adjusted net debt / EBITDA and 46% LTV make the equity a thin, rate-sensitive slice; the tenancy-law reform with an index-rent cap is a live bill in the Bundestag, not a hypothetical; the CEO is new (Jan-2026) and the deleveraging depends on a EUR 2.7bn+ disposal programme in a thin market; and the share price has fallen ~45% from the 2025 close with the last filing (29-Jul-2026) offering no explanation -- the market is telling us something the folder does not yet contain. Base held at 45%: rental income and Adjusted EBITDA guidance were reaffirmed at H1 and the covenant headroom is wide (LTV 45.4% vs 60%, ICR 3.9x vs 1.8x), so the slow-grind base is still the most likely path. Bull cut to 20% because it needs three independent things -- lower Bund yields, benign regulation and disposals at book -- to go right together.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Vonovia on what the equity actually receives -- Adjusted EBT after cash tax, capitalized maintenance and minority payouts (attributable AFFO, EUR 1.26bn / EUR 1.49 per share in FY2025) -- capitalised at a 9% EUR cost of equity, with net debt held at zero because the flow is already after EUR 0.74-0.78bn of interest. EPRA NTA (EUR 46.22 per share) is reported as the cross-check, not the answer: appraised values embed a ~4.0% gross / 2.85% Rental-EBITDA yield that a 9% equity return through 46% LTV cannot carry, so the AFFO value sits at roughly half of NTA and the gap is the model's finding. Fair-value movements, statutory EPS and the CSV free cash flow (after modernization and development spend, before disposal proceeds) are ignored. Growth, modernization and new construction are funded by Recurring Sales, the non-core disposal programme and debt inside the LTV target and are paid for in the model by the organic rent growth path, not deducted a second time as capex.
key_risks_to_valuation: Interest-rate and refinancing exposure: EUR 42bn of debt at ~2.1% average cost repricing ~20bp/yr; each +10bp on the whole stack is ~EUR 42m of Adjusted EBT (~2.2%) and ~EUR 0.05 of AFFO per share
German rent regulation: cabinet tenancy-law bill (April 2026) with a 3% index-rent cap and Kappungsgrenze adjustments is in the legislative process; Mietpreisbremse extended to 2029

Disposal execution: ~EUR 2.7bn non-core German/Swedish assets plus a flagged larger portfolio exit must clear near book for the 40%-LTV-by-2028 target; selling below book shrinks AFFO faster than it cuts interest
Non-controlling-interest payouts rising (143.7 -> 202.9 -> H1 2026 256.0): the Apollo/CBRE IM minority structures carry preferred-style returns that take a growing share of the flow
Unexplained share-price fall of ~23% since the 30-Jun-2026 close with no filing after 29-Jul-2026 in the folder; the Q3 2026 statement (early November) must be read before this valuation is relied on
Cash tax: minimum-tax / RETT share-deal interpretation risk raised to 5-39% probability in the H1 2026 report; the model's 12.5% cash rate assumes the current regime holds
Capitalized maintenance rising faster than rent (+19% in H1 2026) under GModG / EPBD building-energy rules
Equity issuance: the 2025 scrip dividend added 3% to the count; a return to scrip or a rights issue to defend BBB+ would dilute AFFO per share and is not in the flat count

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 15.955-28.90 EUR; a regular Xetra close, not after-hours
data_sources.financials: VNA.DE_Metrics.csv and kpis table (core_metrics, EUR millions) for history; VNA.DE_Annual_FY2025.txt (Adjusted EBT -> OFCF reconciliation, dividend, share count) and VNA.DE_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt (30-Jun-2026 balance sheet, net debt and LTV table, EPRA NTA, FY2026 outlook table, segment Adjusted EBITDA, Opportunities and Risks) for anchors and guidance
